planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring or fall in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil; this Dutch-bred Vuykiana evergreen azalea holds an RHS Award of Garden Merit.

directions: Grow in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, sheltered from harsh winter wind and midday summer sun. Raised by the Vuyk van Nes nursery in Boskoop, the Netherlands, this compact evergreen azalea is one of the Vuykiana group's best-known members, smothering itself each spring in rose-red single flowers over a low, dense mound of foliage. It has held the RHS Award of Garden Merit for its reliability and garden performance in temperate climates. Water during dry spells and trim lightly right after flowering, since next year's buds form soon afterward.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit list

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring or fall in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil; a sister selection to Vuyk's Rosyred, bred by the same Dutch nursery and also an RHS Award of Garden Merit holder.

directions: Plant in acidic, moisture-retentive, well-drained soil in partial shade, giving the shrub room to spread into its mature mound. Bred alongside Vuyk's Rosyred at the Vuyk van Nes nursery in Boskoop, this compact evergreen azalea carries vivid scarlet-red flowers in a dense spring flush and has earned the RHS Award of Garden Merit. It performs reliably in cooler temperate climates where many Southern evergreen azaleas struggle. Keep soil consistently moist during establishment and shape with light pruning immediately after bloom.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit list

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring or fall in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil; a widely grown white-flowered Vuykiana evergreen azalea and RHS Award of Garden Merit holder.

directions: Grow in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, protected from strong wind and intense afternoon sun. This Dutch-raised evergreen azalea bears pure white flowers with a faint pale-green throat marking, held in dense clusters over a broad, mounding evergreen frame, and is regarded as one of the best white evergreen azaleas for small to mid-sized gardens. It carries the RHS Award of Garden Merit for its consistent floral display and garden-worthy habit. Water through dry periods and prune only lightly, right after flowering finishes.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit list

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring or fall in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil; a deep-red Dutch-bred evergreen azalea and RHS Award of Garden Merit holder, often grown for early forced bloom as well as garden display.

directions: Plant in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade, where its compact habit suits foundation plantings and smaller borders. Johanna is a Dutch-bred evergreen azalea prized for its freely produced, deep crimson-red flowers on a dense, low-growing evergreen shrub, and it holds the RHS Award of Garden Merit for reliable garden performance. Its compact size and heavy flowering have also made it a popular choice for pot culture and early-season forcing. Keep soil evenly moist and trim lightly right after flowering to maintain shape.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit list

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring or fall in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil; an early-flowering Kurume-derived evergreen azalea raised by the Blaauw & Co nursery in Boskoop, the Netherlands, and an RHS Award of Garden Merit holder.

directions: Grow in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, allowing the shrub to develop its full rounded size over time. Blaauw's Pink traces to Kurume azalea breeding stock brought to the Netherlands in the early twentieth century, and it is valued for its hose-in-hose, salmon-pink flowers produced in an exceptionally early, heavy spring flush. It has earned the RHS Award of Garden Merit and remains a long-standing favorite among evergreen azaleas for temperate gardens. Water deeply during establishment and prune only right after flowering, since buds for the following season set soon after.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit list

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0) soil in partial shade; a white-flowered Southern Indica azalea that holds the RHS Award of Garden Merit.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade with room for the shrub to reach its large mature size. Niagara is a Southern Indica azalea bearing ruffled white flowers with a faint green throat marking, produced in the same overwhelming spring flush typical of this breeding group, on a large, vigorous evergreen frame. It has been recognized with the RHS Award of Garden Merit for garden-worthy performance and remains a lesser-mined white-flowered counterpart to the more commonly cited Southern Indica selections. Water deeply during dry spells and prune lightly right after flowering, since next year's buds set soon after bloom ends.

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring or fall in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil; a Dutch-bred evergreen azalea noted for unusually blue-toned flowers and an RHS Award of Garden Merit holder.

directions: Grow in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, with protection from strong afternoon sun that can fade flower color. Blue Danube is a Dutch-bred evergreen azalea noted among the Vuykiana group for flowers in an unusually violet-blue shade, a color rarely found in azaleas, held above a dense, rounded evergreen mound. It carries the RHS Award of Garden Merit for its distinctive bloom color and dependable garden performance. Keep soil evenly moist through the growing season and prune lightly immediately after flowering to maintain a compact shape.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit list
